note: The guided tour (O10-O15): Avi and Huey, three doors, the quote builder's names. The script under nodes, Ask's answers under ask, the summary under summary. Off until tour.gate in content/experience.json is "approved"; ?tour=1 previews it. A line's `who` pins it to one guide; every other line is spoken by the lead the visitor picked. Every figure enters through a ref to a sourced manifest field, and names (doors, buyer labels, stages, guides, the builder's offers and programs) are tokens, so none is typed here. `write` puts words on a room's own surfaces (geometry.rooms.<door>.surfaces); `ask` lists Ask's suggested questions for that step. Every text line carries a source and a status; adapted, proposed and derived lines wait for the copy gate (docs/copy-sheets-tour.md, written by tools/tour-text.mjs). Shape: js/tourtext.js. Rules: tools/check-manifest.js.

intro.text: Ask me about 3HUE. I answer only from 3HUE's approved material, and every answer shows where it comes from.

questions.q: What is 3HUE?

lines.text: 3HUE builds and operates security, compliance and AI governance programs for organizations that have to prove their controls work — and have no one inside to run them.
People call when someone with leverage asks for proof: a customer, an auditor, a regulator, an investor. Usually with a date.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §01, the fit model; §04, trigger events

questions.q: Who are {guide:avi} and {guide:huey}?

lines.text: We're your two guides for this lobby. One of us leads and the other stays close, and you chose who leads.

questions.q: How is 3HUE different from a consultant?

lines.text: Two things. 3HUE runs the program instead of handing you a plan, and the same advisor who scopes the work delivers it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §03, three pillars; §05, claims library

lines.text: 3HUE doesn't sell technology. It sells outcomes: a program someone runs, and can prove.
lines.source: 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

questions.q: Where do we start?

lines.text: With no program yet, it is usually the {offer:initial-risk-assessment}. With one in place, a review of what you have. With an exam coming, a {offer:controls-gap-assessment}.
lines.source: 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

lines.text: It begins with a conversation with the team about the obligation in front of you.

questions.q: What should we prepare for an assessment?

lines.text: Very little up front. A first meeting sets the scope, and the analysts work from your existing policies, controls, system inventories and any prior audit reports.
Having people from IT, security and compliance free for short interviews is what speeds it up most.

questions.q: What happens after the first step?

lines.text: Then {ref:arc.1} and {ref:arc.2}. The findings become a prioritized plan with named owners, and if you want 3HUE to run the program, it does.
lines.source: The lobby's three steps; 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); The Ship List §03, landing page copy

lines.text: If you'd rather take the plan and run it yourself, that works too, and you'll have something an internal hire can inherit rather than start over.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

questions.q: Who owns remediation?

lines.text: Accountability stays with you: each gap gets a named owner in the plan of actions and milestones.
3HUE does the heavy lifting. The managed programs track and drive the actions, and 3HUE's engineers can make fixes directly.

questions.q: How is risk prioritized?

lines.text: By business impact, not only technical severity.
The {program:rmp} scores each risk against your risk appetite and your obligations, and records it in the risk register.

questions.q: What is the {program:rmp}?

lines.text: It sets up a risk function that identifies, prioritizes and reduces security risk continuously, with a risk register, assessments and remediation tracking.
It keeps you ready for regulatory reviews and partner due diligence. It's quoted as the {offer:managed-rmp}.
lines.source: 3hue.net, ISG managed programs; 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

questions.q: How do you manage vendor and third-party risk?

lines.text: The {program:vcp} holds vendor practices to your risk tolerance, your contracts and your regulators' expectations.
It keeps vendor assurance audit-ready and checks your highest-risk vendors proactively. It's quoted as the {offer:managed-vcp}.
lines.source: 3hue.net, ISG managed programs; 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

questions.q: What happens during a security incident?

lines.text: The {program:cirp} gives you a plan and incident command: clear roles, escalation paths, coordinated containment and recovery.
Tabletop exercises mean the first real incident isn't the first rehearsal. To start, there's {offer:ir-fast-start}.

For a live incident, 3HUE offers {offer:incident-command}.

questions.q: What does managed detection and response include?

lines.text: Monitoring, detection and response run for you: alerts correlated across your systems, threats hunted, and controls tested.
On the service list it's {offer:mxdr-complete}.

questions.q: What does a virtual CISO do?

lines.text: Executive security leadership that works with your team: it shapes strategy, drives decisions, oversees compliance and owns the board conversation.
lines.source: 3hue.net, ISG managed programs; 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience)

lines.text: How much you use is your call: none, {offer:ciso-support} to build your own capability, or a fractional CISO alongside your team.
lines.source: 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

questions.q: What if we already have a CISO?

lines.text: That's common. The managed programs run alongside your own leadership, and a virtual CISO can mentor an incumbent or take the overflow.

questions.q: Why not just hire a CISO?

lines.text: Eventually you probably should. The question is whether there is a full-time job there yet, or a program that has to exist now.
3HUE runs the program now and builds it so that hire inherits something rather than starting over.
And if what you want is a person rather than a program, say that to the team.

questions.q: Which frameworks do you work with?

lines.text: It depends on who is asking you to prove it. If an examiner is asking, 3HUE works in the frameworks the exam already uses.
lines.source: 3hue.net, framework library; The Forcing Function §04, trigger events

lines.text: If an enterprise buyer is asking, it's usually SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
lines.source: 3hue.net, framework library; The Forcing Function §04, trigger events

lines.text: You'd take {offer:soc-2-readiness} or {offer:iso-27001-readiness}, not both — whichever your buyer named.

questions.q: How long does it take?

lines.text: It depends on the obligation and the date on it.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

lines.text: The first step is scoped to that date, and the plan you get back says how long the rest takes.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

questions.q: How does pricing work?

lines.text: 3HUE doesn't publish list prices. Pricing follows scope and commitment.
Price it against the deal, exam or exit that's waiting on it, not against a tool subscription. For a figure, talk to the team.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling; The Forcing Function §01, the fit model

questions.q: Can I get a quote here?

lines.text: Not on this site. The team builds a quote with you, and your summary names your first step, so that conversation starts there.

questions.q: What's in a package like {offer:soc-2-readiness}?

lines.text: A package bundles the first steps for one obligation. {offer:soc-2-readiness} runs from the {offer:initial-risk-assessment} to the auditor's walkthroughs.
Take {offer:soc-2-readiness} or {offer:iso-27001-readiness}, one or the other, whichever your buyer named. Both sit behind {door:win-trust.title}.
{offer:iso-27701-readiness} and {offer:pci-dss-readiness} sit there too.
{offer:privacy-leadership-launch} is behind {door:gain-control.title}. {offer:ir-fast-start} and {offer:mxdr-complete} are behind {door:stay-ready.title}.

questions.q: Are you the auditor?

lines.text: No. 3HUE prepares you for the auditor and coordinates the walkthroughs. The audit firm issues the report.

questions.q: Our MSP already handles security. Where do you fit?

lines.text: Ask them three questions: which framework are we assessed against, who signs off on risk acceptance, and what happens when an auditor challenges a control?
If the answers are good, you're in fine shape. If they're vague, that's the gap 3HUE fills, alongside your MSP, not instead of it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling; §07, battlecards

questions.q: We already pay for a compliance platform. Why would we need you?

lines.text: Keep it. A platform tells you what's wrong. The question is who fixes it, who answers the questionnaire, and who negotiates scope with the auditor.
That's the job 3HUE does, on top of the tool you already bought.

questions.q: Where does the GRC system run?

lines.text: On your platform, not 3HUE's. {offer:m365-modern-grc-system-deployment-maintenance} stands it up in the tenant you already have.
lines.source: 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

lines.text: If you already run an enterprise GRC platform, 3HUE configures and maintains that instead.
lines.source: 3HUE, Inside 3HUE tour, Ask (3hue.net/experience); 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

questions.q: What is AiVRIC?

lines.text: AiVRIC is the platform 3HUE's managed programs run on, so the evidence stays current between audits instead of being assembled before each one.
lines.source: The Message Stack §09, boilerplate; §01, core narrative

lines.text: The module available today is CloudSignals+RiskOps. Everything else is in development.
lines.source: The Message Stack §05, claims library; 3HUE Brand Sheet §06, naming conventions

questions.q: Isn't this just compliance theater?

lines.text: Mostly, yes. A certificate says controls existed during a window.
That's why 3HUE sells the operating layer, not the certificate: you get the report because your buyer needs it, and a program because you need it.

questions.q: Can you guarantee we pass?

lines.text: No, and be careful with anyone who says otherwise.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

lines.text: What 3HUE can do is tell you before you start whether you'll pass.
Then scope the work to what the standard actually requires, and manage the auditor so there are no surprises.

questions.q: How is this different from a big-firm readiness engagement?

lines.text: Here, the person in the room is the person doing the work, and the scope stays where it was set.
And when the report is delivered, 3HUE is still running the program. Continuity is usually the difference that matters.

questions.q: Our customers are asking how we govern AI. Where do we begin?

lines.text: With four questions: what can it access, what can it change, who approved it, and what proves it stayed inside.
Here the start is {offer:ai-governance-advisory}, built around them.

questions.q: Do you work with private equity portfolios?

lines.text: Yes. For a fund, the first step is the {offer:initial-risk-assessment}, one per company, on the same framework every time.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; 3HUE service catalog, September 2026

questions.q: We have open exam findings. What does the work look like?

lines.text: It starts with a {offer:controls-gap-assessment} on what is actually running, then, under {offer:risk-register-poam}, every finding is tracked until it closes.

questions.q: What proof do you have?
What happens to my answers?

lines.text: This lobby has no sign-up, no analytics and no sign-in. What you type into Ask is matched in this tab and never sent.
lines.source: How this lobby is built: static files, nothing collected

lines.text: Your answers stay in this browser tab, and the summary goes nowhere unless you send it yourself.
lines.source: How this lobby is built: static files, nothing collected

lines.text: If you use the microphone, your browser's own speech service may handle the audio. 3HUE never receives it.
lines.source: How this lobby is built: the browser handles the microphone

questions.q: Nobody has asked us to prove anything yet. Should we talk?

lines.text: Maybe not yet. The trigger is usually a customer, an insurer, an investor or a regulator asking for proof, with a date.
lines.source: The Message Stack §07, battlecards; The Forcing Function §05, who to decline

lines.text: If nobody has asked, you may be early, and 3HUE would rather tell you that than sell you something.
